deities: Lord Shiva (swayambhu Shiv Lingam - self-manifested stone)
festivals: Bala Chaturdashi (November-December; the big mela, drawing devotees across Sikkim and neighbouring states)

history.period: Said to be 1000+ years old (weakly sourced - verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is at Legship in GYALSHING district, NOT in Soreng. Documented with the corrected location. One of Sikkim's few genuinely Hindu temples, the Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple stands on the banks of the Rangeet river at Legship, ~4 km from Pelling on the Geyzing-Pelling route, reached via a footbridge. Legend: pleased with Arjuna's hard penance, Lord Shiva appeared here as the hunter Kirateshwar ('Lord of the Kiratas') and blessed him for the Mahabharata war; a stone miraculously manifesting a Shiv Lingam was later found, and this swayambhu lingam is the main object of worship. Devotees believe a visit with true devotion fulfils wishes - notably for children - and grants peace, health and harmony. Also known as Kirateshwar Mahadev Thaan to the Kirati people; smaller shrines to Rama and Durga stand in the complex. A guest house for devotees stands on site.

name: Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
town: Legship, Gyalshing district (CSV town 'Soreng' is WRONG)
town_description: Legship is a small town on the Rangeet river in Gyalshing district, West Sikkim, on the Geyzing-Pelling tourist route (~4 km from Pelling). The temple sits below the main road on the riverbank, reached by a footbridge and steps; the river setting and forested hills make it one of Sikkim's most scenic pilgrimage spots.

travel.airport: Pakyong Airport - about 100 km (verify); Siliguri/Bagdogra is the main air gateway.
travel.road: Day trip from Pelling (~4 km) or Geyzing; footbridge from the main road to the temple; local taxis and shared vehicles (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid monsoon (river access can be risky). Bala Chaturdashi (Nov-Dec) is the grandest but crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Widely reported as 6:00 AM-7:00 PM (verify). Daily Vedic puja with morning/evening aarti; dress modestly, remove footwear before the sanctum.
